$comment: D-FFI-DARWIN-SYSCTL-CONSTANTS-EMPTY — the gate-resident RUNTIME witness for the Darwin sysctl MIB constants in src/dss-config/shippedLibs/sys/sysctl.json. WHY IT EXISTS: shipping CTL_HW/HW_NCPU/HW_AVAILCPU is what lets sqlite's src/test1.c:9100-9104 compile for macho, but a wrong MIB number compiles just as happily — the descriptor SHADOWS the SDK's <sys/sysctl.h> totally (include_path_resolve.hpp: Descriptor beats Source), so nothing in the build offers a second opinion; the program would just query a different kernel node and return a plausible number. A value table cannot self-check, so the only instrument left is the kernel, and that is what main.c asks. The unit test tests/ffi RealSysSysctlJsonMibConstantDomains is this example's structural twin and pins the DECLARED numbers; only this arm proves they BIND to the nodes their names claim. THE SINGLE INCLUDE IS THE POINT: main.c includes <sys/sysctl.h> and nothing else, so every name in it — both functions and every constant — can only have come from that one descriptor. The sibling shipped_flock_statfs_sysctl_zone_macho reaches sysctl through <unistd.h> and #defines CTL_HW/HW_PAGESIZE in its own source, so it witnesses the CALL and says nothing about these constants; this example covers exactly that hole. HERMETIC: no core count, memory size, page size or path is compared to a literal — only nodes against each other plus bounds true on any Mac (counts positive, availcpu <= ncpu, page size a positive power of two, the CTLTYPE_QUAD node wider than an int node). Nothing touches disk. The page size is deliberately never pinned: MEASURED, the same physical Mac reports 16384 to an arm64 binary and 4096 to an x86_64 one. Exit 42 = lenNcpuMib 4 + lenMemMib 8 + rcAbsent -1 + four cross-form deltas 0 + nine success rcs 0 + 31, and it cannot fold: the guards (1..23) prove only liveness and ordering — nonzero, positive, wider, failed — while the two kernel-written lengths, the exact -1 and all four deltas are asserted ONLY in the return expression, every operand an opaque extern return or a cell the kernel wrote through an out-param. THE STRONGEST CHECK is the WIDTH discriminator: hw.memsize is CTLTYPE_QUAD, so the kernel writes back length 8 where every int node writes 4 — a HW_MEMSIZE pointing at any int-typed sibling is caught by the LENGTH alone, independently of the value, and that is a property of the node's type rather than of the hardware. ⚠ THE WEAK SPOT, STATED: HW_AVAILCPU is pinned only by rc 0, a positive count and availcpu <= ncpu, because MEASURED there is NO name-addressable hw.availcpu node (sysctlbyname returns -1 on both arches while the MIB form succeeds), so the cross-check every other constant here gets is unavailable for that one; on a machine where availcpu == ncpu a HW_AVAILCPU wrongly equal to HW_NCPU would not be caught. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete any constant row main.c names → error[S0001] at its use and no binary; perturb a value instead and the build still succeeds while the RUN fails, at a numbered guard or on the exit code. The macho-only target is DELIBERATE and not an oversight: the whole descriptor is availableObjectFormats [macho], so an elf/pe #include of <sys/sysctl.h> fails loud with F001D (verified) and an ungated arm could not compile at all — the single arm64-macho target IS the whole honest surface (the shipped_flock_statfs_sysctl_zone_macho / shipped_strlcpy_strlcat_macho shape). The x86_64-macho arm was compile-verified and Rosetta-run-verified while authoring but is NOT declared: it would make the example depend on Rosetta existing on whatever host runs the darwin leg. The release arm re-runs every call under the full optimizer.
